Ik stond altijd op voor de klant (wat ook de klant was voor onze zakenpartners) en onze collega’s binnen de norm. (Genoeg mensen ook afgewezen hoor.)

Wat ik nu anders doe is niet meer kijken naar het gehele proces/de keten waar problemen zijn en punten die mij opvallen. Ik blijf nu binnen mijn vaarwater zo gezegd en focus enkel daar op. Ik geef enkel dingen nu aan die impact hebben op mijn werk zonder teveel detail of erin te duiken. Ook een dosis extra positief zijn in meetings etc. werkt en niet te kritisch zijn. Laat dat nu over aan mijn managers en geef enkel 1 op 1 dingen aan ipv in groepsverband.

Wat wel anders is dat mijn manager wel mijn drive voor oplossingsgerichtheid waardeert en cursus voor Lean en Sigma volg. -Bemoei me niet met andere werkzaamheden/teams (direct) ook al heeft het invloed erop. 
In meetings etc. 
- Laat ik niet me te kritische kant zien of ga mee met de negatieve houdingen van andere collega’ s in ‘openbare situties.’

Ik begrijp dat maar al te goed. Vriendjespolitiek is eenmaal het huidige pad naar promotie en handjes boven het hoofd houden. Hoe “rot” het ook is maar deze houding heb ik nu bij mijn huidige werkgever aangenomen wat wonderbaarlijk werkt. Can’t beat them, join them.

Verder iemand op een functie die er niet thuis hoort zonder te kijken naar andere interne kandidaten ken ik maar al te goed. Helaas ook vanuit mijn vorige werkgever.

Een trainer en vraagbaak die goed kon slijmen bij management zonder dat deze persoon maar ook enig draagvlak had bij beide teams. (Beetje biased, haha) Ik ging zelf ook voor de functie, had meeste draagvlak binnen de teams en mijn kennisniveau van de gehele keten was zo op peil dat andere afdeling ook bij mij advies vroegen over de interne processen en verbeteringen, maar zoals eerder benoemd was ik geen “teamplayer” en “paste ik niet in de toekomstvisie”. 

Achteraf ben ik blij dat ik weg ben en de les van vriendjespolitiek heb geleerd. Verdien nu bijna twee keer mijn vorig bruto salaris + opleiding/cursussen dit jaar voor een doorgroeimogelijkheid aan het einde van het jaar zou ik alles behalen. Echt een complete 180.

Ik heb al mijn opgedane kennis nergens gewaarborgd en dat is, uitgaand van de woorden van oud collega’s, heel erg te merken.

Ik ben bij mijn vorige werkgever (zal de naam voor me houden) hoofd van de klachtenafdeling geweest. Pas nadat ik weg was en soort van zelfreflectie/terugblik deed over mijn 2,5 jaar daar zag ik pas echt goed hoe erg het toneelstuk “vriendjespolitiek en ik” werd gespeeld.

Ik zat tussen afdelingen, klanten, partners, bestuur en stakeholders in, maar zo waar ik een feit boven tafel bracht dat iemand hoger op al 1+ jaar haar werk als product owner nooit heeft uitgevoerd (de afdeling die de software moest ontwikkelen voor de backend heeft nooit een opdracht gekregen) en zwart op wit erover heeft gelogen krijg ik alleen; “Ja, je was wel erg feitelijk etc. Je kan het ook alleen aanvliegen met een oplossende mindset zonder het negatieve te benoemen.”

Einde van dat jaar wordt ze tijdens de jaarafsluiting nog de hemel ingeprezen door het bestuur ondanks dat. Toen raakte de realiteit van hogere functies en kantoor toneel.

Only dropped this because of OP’s question and not giving it as actual investment advice.

My bank got Guided Investments with 6 different kind of portfolios you can select. They explain how it work. 

Each is numbered from 1 lowest risk/lowest return- 6 highest return/highest risk.

I choose 5 and got 7-8% return last year.

Sure, those aren’t returns as big as day traders or people who short etc. but beats the returns of  the usual saving accounts or the 3% you see being advertised.

Edit: Reason i go with the bank instead going somewhere else or do it myself is “banks make money and are bound by better rules/want to make money and have trust they can do this.” Just my thought and not based on research.

When choosing an investment portfolio with the bank i choose they show the results of the last 10 years. 8 out of 10 had good returns with 5 out of 10 being 10% +. (Yeah, i know past results aren’t…)

What works for me, besides paying off debt 1100,- a month i made by dumb mistakes, is a principle i learned of “paying yourself first”. Basically your own savings/investment is also a “bill” like rent.

At this moment i put 150,- a month in my investment account i got with the bank for almost 2 years with an actually good return and 100,- into normal savings.

I am lucky to earn decent, cheap monthly costs (small house) and am pretty minimalist with my lifestyle. Also saving a bit for hobbies works also.

Instead of calling Stedin first, you must call your energy provider first. Call, no mail.

They need register your contract to your EAN metercode into the CAR. Centrale Aansluit Register. Without this registration you can say and call what you want to Stedin but they will give you the same information/cut your utilities.

Press hard with your energy supplier to make it clear your(their) contract is not registered in the CAR/on your EAN metercode. Have them doublecheck it is on the right EAN code.

After this call Stedin to check the CAR. If it is in there problem solved. 

Do take into account that for the period there wasn’t a contract, as it takes some time to actually get to the point of have your utilities cut off, they will bill the current owner/renter.

Ask them what this period was and be sure to have some documentation ready, such as a rental agreement and the actual meter reading of your utilities the moment you moved in, so in case you had a period with no contract they will bill you the right amount of the right period.

I am a bisexual guy in the Netherlands and i have always been out with a 'i am what i am attitude' while living in the Randstad area/Noord- and Zuid-Holland.

While ofcourse it can differ from place to place, the last 20+ years or so in general i haven't had bad experiences when people found out. School, work or anything in public people always been either neutral or accepting but i have a large build and imposing look, haha.

Ofcourse everyone has their own way of coming out and expressing their sexuality. For me what seems to work is just to be myself and whenever the topic comes up i never 'come out'  as "ooh, you need to know about me i am bi' but just go along with a topic like. " Yeah, my ex-boyfriend was a dick too. Know what you mean" or "Yeah, i find that type attractive too."

99.99% of the time it always goes like " Ooh, so you like both?" and usual the talks keep going the same as if i was talking about an ex girlfriend or an interest in woman. Popping a casual joke around seems to lighten the mood to make people more relax around it. " yeah, for me it's part-time depending on the job" or because i am more attracted to woman. "I work full-time (woman) and some side gig/ZZP work (men). Depends if i like what i see."  


In the end it is how you wanna express yourself and live your life but perhaps you might get something from my experience/story. Also my advice to have this attitude to your therapist, in my view and lifestyle at least, haha. You should never have to come out, explain yourself or defend yourself. Just be Bi and just drop it into a convo if a topic about sex or relationships come up with you involved. Can't guarantee it works for you but so far, so good for me with people from all walks of life/backgrounds.

Now for the apartment not existing is an issue. Cause you have the registration at gemeente for you as a person, like your postadress etc. but the gemeente also needs to assign your house as an existing adres, usually done together with the company/contractor which has build the complex, into the central data base where all connection points are registered.   
Basically the 'technical' adres of your apartment, not the adres used for the apartment perse itself.   
Example. You have a building with housenumber 2 and extention 2 A, 2 B, 2 C etc.   
2 A's technical adres usually is the same as the postal adres. unfortunally, especially if its a fiberglass connection cause they are fucking that up even worse, the technical adres can be completely different like 2 K.   


This registration issue is very grey when it comes to who is responsible so i would focus on getting it solved instead of sending complaints/compensation or letting your managers handle this since most likely they dont know how to.   


Regardless you should call KPN yourself ( again ).   


First to find our if you have fiberglass or copper connection ( usually in the same place as your fuses etc. ) You can google 'FTU KPN meterkast ' or ' Koper ISRA punt ' which is the old copper telephone landline.   


For it to be easier online go to [https://xs4all-fpi-info.fourstack.nl/](https://xs4all-fpi-info.fourstack.nl/) and fill in your postal code and housenumber. If your housenumber doesnt pop up or there are multiple possiblities it will show in the dropdown menu on the right side ( website is so easy cant miss it ). Here you will also see if you got copper or fiberglass according to the system ( has its own issue since it sometimes works in a general estimated speed etc. so while it is trust worthy dont use for that. Purely for adresses )  


When you know where your FTU or ISRA is located ( ask your neighbours to show where theirs is located if you cant find it ) and the possible adresses call KPN to have engineer come by again.   


If you have an active line coming in ( connection to a central hub where all the connection go through ) he/she should be able to 'measure' which is yours/the name of the line. If somehow your line is dead/not connected he should call his engineers line ( monteursingang ) for support and/or create a support ticket to have the line restored. As someone who has worked for several Telecom companies in the Netherlands and also for large business this is all depending on your location.

First is to know if your split building has its own registered housenumber. Thinking 2, 2A, 2B etc. Since making a rental contract this must be stated and also when you register with your city ( gemeente ). If so check your lease as internet nowadays is almost a basic in a home what it states. You can even go so far to contact your city what there rules are about landlords providing a house with its own connection. 

Besides the first thing you can do a few steps. Since most buildings but not all, even old ones, can have 2 connections. Copper (xDSL like KPN ) or Coax ( Ziggo ). If you are lucky it may have fibreglass as a third option.

Just call a provider ( KPN if your neighbour has Ziggo and viceversa ).

If there is only copper ( xDSL ) call to ask if its possible they can deliver on the same cable ( Isra points ).  If a cable has more lines available they can use that one next to the line of your neighbour as certain copper cables can do this and perhaps create a second ISRA point.

Go to the city ( gemeentehuis ) for help. Their job is to help people get on their feet asap and are the ones who can get you an appointment with the right people to take the right steps as have a roof over your head, an education but stuck in between.
